title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from pages 649–651: Grothendieck builds a 'schematic envelope' Env(𝔊) for a discrete group 𝔊 that is virtually abelian. He calls such groups 'virtabéliens': they contain a finite-index subgroup that is commutative and finitely generated (torsion-free) as a Z-module. Env(𝔊) is a pro-system of affine group schemes over S_0 = Spec Z, indexed by the normal subgroups M ⊂ 𝔊 that are commutative and torsion-free.

How each term is built. For a lattice M ≅ Z^r, the envelope is the vector group M ⊗ G_a. He writes this as Z̲ = G_a when M = Z. Given 1 → M → 𝔊 → 𝔊/M → 1, one pushes the extension out along M → M ⊗ G_a. The result 𝔊_M is an extension of the finite constant group scheme (𝔊/M)_{S_0} by the vector group.

What the page settles.
- He first fixes the sense of exactness claimed for (49). The text is partly illegible, but it apparently means exactness as sheaves for a faithfully flat topology on the base, for connected group schemes and their limits.
- He says the general case reduces 'quasi immédiatement' to the typical case 𝔊 = M = Z, with the exact sequences (50) 1 → Z --n--> Z → Z/nZ → 1.
- He makes 𝔊_n explicit: the pushout of (50) along Z → G_a, i.e. 𝔊_n = (G_a × Z)/{(k, −nk)}, an extension of (Z/n)_{S_0} by G_a.
- 𝔊_n is affine. Its coordinate ring is isomorphic, non-canonically, to the product of n copies of Z[T]. The isomorphism comes from choosing a set-theoretic section of Z → Z/n, e.g. {0, …, n−1}.
- The group law, begun at the bottom of the page, is then (i,t)·(j,s) = (i+j, t+s) if i+j < n, and (i+j−n, t+s+1) otherwise. This is a carry cocycle.

What the next page adds.
- The transition maps 𝔊_{nm} → 𝔊_n are not flat.
- The projective limit is a 'schematization' of the profinite group Ẑ_{S_0}.
- Its neutral component is Spec of colim Z[T/n] = Z + T·Q[T], the polynomials in Q[T] with integer constant term. Grothendieck calls this 'chose étrange'.
- There is an analogue Z^r + (higher terms) for Z^r.
errors: The text gives no gaps in the mathematics. The pushout description and the n-copies-of-Z[T] description are correct.
The exactness claim (49) is stated only 'en un sens qu'il conviendrait de préciser'. It needs fpqc/fppf sheaf exactness, and care with limits, since the transition maps are not flat.

Worth noting, and not on the page: the neutral component of the limit is Spec(Z + TQ[T]). Over F_p this fibre is a single point, because TQ[T] ⊗ F_p = 0. Over Q it is G_a. So the envelope is highly non-flat in an interesting way; Grothendieck only flags the ring as 'strange'.

ideas.what: Schematic/algebraic envelope over Spec Z of a virtually abelian discrete group, as a pro-affine group scheme, via pushout along M → M⊗G_a.
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic hull / pro-algebraic (Zariski) completion of virtually polycyclic groups, here over Z rather than Q
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mostow (algebraic hull, over Q); Hochschild–Mostow (pro-algebraic completion); later Toën and others (schematic homotopy types)
ideas.where_published: Not in the published part of La Longue Marche as far as I know; this sequel (pp. 650 bis–787) is unpublished

ideas.what: Explicit description of the extension of (Z/n) by G_a pushed out from 1→Z→Z→Z/n→1: coordinate ring ≅ Z[T]^n via a section, group law given by a carry cocycle.
ideas.modern_name: Pushout of extensions / Ext^1(Z/n, G_a) over Spec Z; carry cocycle

ideas.what: Reduction of the general virtually abelian case to 𝔊 = M = Z.

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches an integral (over Spec Z) pro-algebraic envelope of virtually abelian, and implicitly virtually polycyclic, groups. Its limit yields a schematization of Ẑ_{S_0} whose identity component is Spec(Z + TQ[T]). Envelopes of this kind are classically studied over fields of characteristic 0; an integral version with this degenerate behaviour at primes does not appear standard.
missed.quote: je vais expliciter la construction de l'extension correspondante de Z/nZ par Z̲ = G_a … C'est un schéma affine, dont l'anneau des coordonnées est isomorphe — de façon pas bien canonique — au produit de n copies de celui de Z̲ = G_a, savoir Z[T]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This bears on integral models of schematic homotopy types and affine group schemes over Z. It relates to the anabelian programme of La Longue Marche, i.e. schematizing discrete/profinite fundamental groups, where integral structure is still subtle. The non-flat Hopf algebra Z + TQ[T] is a concrete test object.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is an elementary explicit computation. Its interest is the unpublished programme it belongs to: an integral 'Env' of virtually abelian groups linking discrete groups, Ẑ and non-Noetherian Hopf algebras over Z. This seems not to be developed in the literature in this form, but it is not a deep finished result.
transcription_corrections: Line 3 likely reads 'connexes (obtenus par passage à la limite)'; the '(et même [?]' reading is doubtful.
'G = M = Z' should be Gothic 𝔊 = M = Z, the group 𝔊 of the previous page.
'Z̲ = G_a' is Grothendieck's notation for the envelope of Z, i.e. the vector group G_a (underlined Z). The extension is of Z/nZ by G_a, and its name is 𝔊_n (Gothic).
The 25 at the bottom left is the archive page number.
